1 ISSUE
2
3 BRYDON, Chair --Does a parcel whose current use classification is
4 derived through its " integral" link to a noncontiguous but commonly
5 owned farm parcel retain its farm and agricultural land classification
6 on sale of the farm parcel to a separate owner, there being no change
7 to the " integral" link between the properties after the sale?
8
9 We conclude that where the integral relationship of the parcels
10 is unchanged upon sale, there is no requirement to alter the current
11 use classification, solely due to the change in ownership.
12
13 FACTS
14
15 The facts are not in dispute and are summarized as follows. The
16 subject property is a five -acre parcel located on Sorenson Road in
17 Kittitas County, Assessor' s Parcel No. 17- 20- 2000- 0012. The parcel is
18 unimproved other than for boundary fencing and work done in 1986 to
19 develop an existing artesian spring to meet county standards for a
20 public water supply.
21
22 Prior to February 1984, Owner owned both this parcel and, with a
23 co- owner, a second, 175 -acre property known as Willow Springs Ranch
24 Ranch)' located approximately one- quarter mile to the west. 2 The two

4 CONTENTIONS
5
6 The Assessor' s central contention is that on sale of the Ranch,
7 the subject property is no longer part of a farming operation. The
8 Ranch is under different ownership from the subject parcel. There-
9 fore, the subject does not qualify for current use classification as
10 farm and agricultural land, absent a showing by Owner of income
11 derived from his retained parcel, as required by RCW 84. 34. 020( 2). 3
12 The Assessor suggests that Owner apply for a current use classifi-
13 cation as farm and agriculture conservation lands, noting the tax
14 consequences are the same under either classification.
15
16 Initially, the Assessor contended Owner had not shown farm income
17 from the subject parcel. However, Owner said he does not claim farm
18 income for this parcel. He believes this misunderstanding arises from
19 the County Board' s decision imputing an income to the Owner out of an
20 arrangement with the current Ranch owner to mend fences and control
21 weeds on the subject parcel. In any event, the parties now agree on
22 this issue; it is no longer in dispute.
23
24 Owner begins his argument by citing the historic link between the
25 subject parcel with its water source, the Ranch, and the surrounding

25 5 "` Appurtenance' refers to something used with, and related to or dependent upon
another thing; that is, something that belongs to something else, an adjunct. The
thing appurtenant is strictly necessary and essential to the proper use and enjoyment
26
of the land, as well as useful or necessary for carrying out the purposes for which

27 6 "' Contiguous' means land that adjoins other land that is owned by the same owner or

1 ANALYSIS AND CONCLUSIONS
2
3 We begin our analysis with the Assessor' s central contention that
4 on sale of the Ranch, the retained subject property is no longer part
5 of a farming operation.
6
7 Current use farm and agricultural classification is determined
8 by a parcel' s use, its size, its gross income, or some combination
9 thereof. RCW 84. 34. 020( 2) defines "[ f)arm and agricultural land" as
10 follows:
11 a) Any parcel of land that is twenty or more acres
or multiple parcels of land that are contiguous and total
12 twenty or more acres:
i) Devoted primarily to the production of livestock
13 or agricultural commodities for commercial purposes;
ii) Enrolled in the federal conservation reserve
14 program or its successor administered by the United States
department of agriculture; or
15 iii) Other similar commercial activities as may be
established by rule . . . .
16
17 The subject parcel does not satisfy these criteria.
18
19 The definitions continue:
20 b) Any parcel of land that is five acres or more but
less than twenty acres devoted primarily to agricultural
21 uses, which has produced a gross income from agricultural
uses equivalent to . . .
22
ii) On or after January 1, 1993, two hundred dollars
23 or more per acre per year for three of the five calendar
years preceding the date of application for classification
24 under this chapter . . . .
25
26 The parties agree the subject parcel does not generate any income
27 from agricultural use.

1 Subparagraph ( c) applies to parcels of less than five acres and,
2 therefore, is not relevant to this case. Continuing:
3 d) Any lands including incidental uses as are
compatible with agricultural purposes, including wetlands
4 preservation, provided such incidental use does not exceed
twenty percent of the classified land and the land on which
5 appurtenances necessary to the production, preparation, or
sale of the agricultural products exist in conjunction with
6 the lands producing such products. Agricultural lands shall
also include any parcel of land of one to five acres, which
7 is not contiguous, but which otherwise constitutes an
integral part of farming operations being conducted on land
8 qualifying under this section as " farm and agricultural
lands" . . . .
9
10 The first sentence in this paragraph does not apply to the case
11 before us. However, the second sentence is pertinent. " Agricultural
12 lands shall also include any parcel of land of one to five acres,
13 which is not contiguous, but which otherwise constitutes an integral
14 part of farming operations being conducted on land qualifying under
15 this section as ' farm and agricultural lands'." ( Emphasis added.)
16
17 Is the subject property with its sole source , water supply
18 integral" to operation of the Ranch? " Integral" is defined in WAC
19 458- 30- 200( 2)( y), as follows: "` Integral' means that which is central
20 to or inherent in the use or operation of classified farm and agri-
21 cultural land for commercial agricultural purposes."
22
23 The Ranch is classified as open space farm and agricultural land.
24 Testimony established that the Ranch does not have an independent
25 source of water within its boundary. Testimony also established that
26 various water drilling efforts during the 20th Century failed to locate
27 a source of water on the Ranch property and no other water supply,

1 public or private, serves the Ranch. And, finally, testimony estab-
2 lished that the Ranch property has relied and continues to be entirely
3 dependent on the subject parcel' s artesian well for its domestic,
4 farm, and agricultural water requirements.
5
6 It is axiomatic that farm and agriculture operations are
7 dependent on a viable water source. No water, no farm. The testimony
8 and exhibits establish that no other water supply exists to meet the
9 needs of the Ranch. The testimony and exhibits also establish the
10 subject parcel is not contiguous to the Ranch, the Owner' s contrary
11 contention on that point having failed the test of the definition he
12 cites in WAC 458- 30- 200( 2)( n).' Further, the statute sets no require-
13 ment of common ownership of the noncontiguous parcels. Therefore, the
14 Board concludes that subject parcel with its sole source water supply
15 is central to the farming operations conducted on the Ranch and,
16 therefore, an integral part of farming operations conducted on land
17 classified as open space farm and agricultural lands.
18
19 The Board concludes the sale of one of two commonly owned
20 properties does not necessarily sever the integral connection between
21 two parcels for purposes of open space classification. Rather, an
22 assessor must review all the facts to determine if the elements that
23 provide the integral link between the parcels prior to sale continue
24 following sale. On that basis, the Board concludes subject parcel

1 remains integral to the Ranch and is correctly classified as open
2 space farm and agricultural land pursuant to RCW 84. 34. 020( 2). The
3 future development of a water source within the Ranch boundary or the
4 provision of a public or alternative private water supply to the Ranch
5 could alter this classification but that is a matter to be resolved at
6 such time when it arises. For the issue before this Board today, the
7 decision of the County Board is affirmed.

10 CONCLUSIONS OF LAW
11
12 1. 0 This Board has jurisdiction over the persons and subject
13 matter of this proceeding.
14
15 2. 1 By Chapter 84. 34 RCW, the Legislature established an open
16 space, agricultural, and timber land current use conservation program
17 setting the policy, establishing eligibility criteria, setting proce-
18 dural parameters, and delegating to the Department of Revenue neces-
19 sary rulemaking authority for the program.
20
21 2. 2 Farm and agricultural lands include any parcel of land of
22 one to five acres, which is not contiguous, but which otherwise
23 constitutes an integral part of farming operations being conducted on
24 land qualifying as " farm and agricultural lands". RCW 84. 34. 020( 2).
25
26 3. 0 Land constituting an integral part of farming operations is
27 land which is critical to or inherent in the use or operation of

1 classified farm and agricultural land for commercial agricultural
2 uses. WAC 458- 30- 200( 2)( y).
3
4 4. 0 The spring located on the subject property is the sole
5 source of water for the Ranch. This water source is encumbered in
6 favor of the Ranch as the first and paramount user by a recorded
7 Contract of Sale binding upon the current and future owners of the
8 subject. Consequently, this sole source water supply is ." integral"
9 to the successful operation of the classified farm and agricultural
10 land identified as the Ranch. Therefore, the subject is properly
11 classified as open space farm and agricultural land pursuant to RCW
12 84. 34. 020 (2) .
